# The design system — noddo

> **The product is noddo** — the product and the company (owner, 2026-11-03). Its design system is the
> package the owner's designers delivered on 2026-11-03, vendored verbatim into
> **`hris/styles/noddo/`**: `SPEC.md` (the rules), `tokens.json` / `tokens.css` (the values), `icons.md`
> and `fonts.md`, and `PACKAGE_README.md` (which file wins when two disagree: SPEC for rules, tokens for
> values). The whole frontend was moved onto it on 2026-11-04 (`HISTORY.md` § "The redesign onto noddo");
> this page says **how the package is wired into the code**, so a new screen follows it without
> re-deriving anything. It replaces the "design direction" note of 2026-10-16, which asked for a calm,
> modern product out of the old kit; the package is that direction made concrete.

**Read `SPEC.md` before building a screen.** The rest of this folder — menus, tables, status, forms,
naming — is the product's own settled answers, and where it and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins and the rule
here is changed (it happened to Title Case: `NAMING.md` § 1).

## 1. Where everything is

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The rules and values | `hris/styles/noddo/` — never edited by hand; a new package version replaces the files |
| The one stylesheet | `hris/styles/globals.css` — imports Tailwind, then `tokens.css` unlayered, then maps the tokens onto Tailwind's theme |
| The component kit ("Desact") | `hris/components/desact/` — **our code since 2026-11-04**, rewritten to SPEC; it was a vendored shadcn copy under `public/desact` and nobody could touch it |
| Brand | `hris/components/brand/` — `NoddoWordmark`, `NoddoMark`, `PoweredByNoddo`; the only files that hard-code Wine and Rose |
| Illustrations | `hris/components/illustrations/` — the 59 ring scenes as React, `<Illustration scene size>`, generated from the SVGs in `hris/styles/noddo/assets/illustrations/` by `npm run illustrations` (never edited by hand); the 404 page's moving drawing is `<NotFoundDrawing>` |
| Accent | `hris/lib/theme/accent.ts`; on the server `AccentColors` / `AccentPreset` (`hris-api/…/entities/`) |
| Tag palette | `hris/lib/theme/tags.ts`; on the server `TagColor` |
| Leave palette | `hris/lib/theme/leave.ts` — the `--leave-*` tokens in `globals.css` (§ 7) |
| Fonts | `hris/styles/fonts/fonts.ts` — Inter, Inter Tight, JetBrains Mono through `next/font/google` |
| The fence | `hris/test/designSystemGuard.test.ts` and the `RAW_HUE` rule in `hris/eslint.config.mjs` |

## 2. Tailwind knows only the system

`globals.css` switches Tailwind's own defaults off (`--color-*: initial`, the same for radius, shadow,
text size, font, weight, tracking, animation, easing) and declares the system's names in
`@theme inline reference`. So:

- **An old class produces no CSS at all** — `bg-brown-50`, `text-sm`, `rounded-lg`, `shadow-md`,
  `font-bold`. Nothing in the browser says so; the guard test does.
- The names are SPEC's roles: text `text-primary | secondary | tertiary | disabled | on-inverse`;
  surfaces `bg-page | card | subtle | mist | canvas | inverse | row-hover`; borders `border-divider |
  field | strong`; the accent family `bg-accent`, `text-accent-text`, `bg-accent-subtle`, `ring-accent-ring`;
  status `bg-status-<tone>-bg|fill`, `text-status-<tone>-text|icon`, `border-status-<tone>-border`;
  tags `bg-tag-<colour>-bg|bar`, `text-tag-<colour>-text`; leave `bg-leave-<colour>-fill|edge`,
  `text-leave-<colour>-text`, `border-leave-<colour>-edge` (through `LEAVE_CLASSES`, never typed by hand).
- Type is a role too, size, line height, tracking and weight together: `text-greeting`, `text-page-title`,
  `text-section-title`, `text-card-title`, `text-body`, `text-label`, `text-hint`, `text-number`,
  `text-code`. Weights are `font-normal | medium | semibold` — no 700, no light, no italics, no capitals.
- Radii and shadows are levels: `rounded-tag | control | popover | card | panel | pill` (and
  `rounded-glyph`, the 4 px row checkbox); `shadow-card | raised | popover | dialog | drag`.
- `tailwind-merge` is taught the same lists (`hris/lib/cn.ts`), or it would merge `text-body` with
  `text-primary` and drop one.

`tokens.css` stays **unlayered**, so it outranks Tailwind's layers, and a role that the accent drives is
re-declared on any element with `data-theme` or `data-accent` — which is how the Appearance preview is
an island in the draft colour inside a page in the saved one.

## 3. The workspace accent

A company picks one of nine presets — Wine, Cherry, Tangerine, Sunflower, Basil, Indigo, Ocean, Mulberry, Black —
or a custom HEX (`company_appearance.accent`: a preset's name, `graphite`, kept as a value off the grid, or
`#rrggbb`; sign-in-appearance, 2026-11-13). A light colour writes Graphite on its fill, decided by contrast. Until
the package carries the nine (agreed 2026-11-18 — the designers ship them in the next version), the presets it lacks are derived like a custom colour. A
red workspace (`isRedAccent`) puts `data-accent-tone="red"` beside the accent, and the confirm dialog's destructive
button becomes a red outline. The root layout reads it on the server and puts `data-accent` — or, for a custom colour, the
derived inputs in `style` — on `<html>`, so the first frame is already in the company's colour. A
custom colour is made readable the way the package's `accent.js` does it; `accent.ts` is that code in
TypeScript and its test proves it reproduces every preset the package carries. Java has the same derivation
(`AccentColors`), for what the server paints itself — an email's button.

**The accent changes everything accent and nothing else** (SPEC § 2): the primary and Approve buttons,
links, focus, selection, the active navigation item, the selected row and tab, toggles, the illustration
ring, the loader, "today" on a calendar, the first chart series. Greys, text, status colours, the tag
palette, fonts, radii and icons are always noddo's — Approved is Pine and an error is red in every
workspace.

## 4. Two brands, never side by side

On a company's address the company is primary: its logo and colour on sign-in, reset, invitation,
preboarding and in its emails, and noddo only as "powered by noddo" at the foot. On the root —
the landing site, the trial, "find your company" — and in the setup wizard every screen is noddo's.
Inside the app noddo does not appear in the chrome (the owner, 2026-11-05 — § 7). The name is always lower case.

**A page in the company's brand ends with one footer** — the guest signing page and its states, the phone drawing
page, a new joiner's signing page (`hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-17-documents/PRODUCT-RULES.md`, taken by the owner on 2026-11-18):
- one line, **"Signing powered by noddo"** on a signing page (never just "Powered by"); the noddo part is the grey
  wordmark image, 15 high, never typed;
- centred on the page, 44 high, hint style in tertiary grey, 5 px before the wordmark, the wordmark lifted 1 px so
  its letters sit on the text's line.

**A phone page opened from a QR code** has the company colour band on top with the logo, white below, no rings, and
the same footer.

## 5. The components that carry the rules

A rule that is not a component drifts, so these are the only ways to draw what they draw:

| Need | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| A status | `StatusBadge` (nine tones, always icon + word) and the entity wrappers | a coloured span |
| A user-chosen colour | `TagChip`, the tag palette by name | a HEX, a status colour |
| A field's error | `FieldError` (`desact/field-error`) under the field | a red `<p>` |
| A form's refusal | `FormError` → `InlineAlert tone="declined"` | a red box |
| A message inside a form | `InlineAlert` (approved, pending, declined, info) | a hand-painted panel |
| The state of a page | `Banner` — neutral Mist, never yellow or red | an amber strip |
| Waiting | `NodRing` (or `Loader`), `Skeleton` with shimmer, a button's `loading` | a spinner, three dots, "Loading…" text |
| Empty, error, 404/403/500 | `EmptyState`, `ErrorState`, `ErrorPage` — each with an illustration | an icon in a circle |
| Wizard progress | `Stepper` / `StepRing` | "Step 1 of 2" text alone |
| A list of steps a person goes through (who approves, who signs) | the step rule below | done told apart by colour alone |
| A date, a range of dates | `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker` (`components/ui/DatePicker`, on `desact/calendar`) — FORMS_AND_FIELDS.md § 8 | `<input type="date">`, a hand-built calendar popover |
| Picking one option from a menu | `ChoiceMenu` (`desact/choice-menu`) — ACTIONS_AND_MENUS.md § 10 | a check column on the left, a radio dot |
| Several picked values in a closed field | `FittedNames` (`components/ui/FittedNames`) — "Design, Sales +1" | the whole list cut with … |
| A choice filter | `FilterChip` | a toggle button |
| Filtering a list by conditions | `FilterPopover` (`components/audience/`) — the Filter button, the 620 popover, the applied chips | a popover of hand-laid builder rows |
| The conditions themselves | `AudienceBuilder` (`layout="line"` in a popover or dialog, `"stacked"` in a ~320–400 panel; `actions` makes it a popover body with a fixed foot) | rows of 36-high selects |
| One condition's look | `ConditionCard`, `ConditionJoiner` ("and"), `AddConditionButton`, `CompactSelect`, `compactTrigger` (`components/audience/ConditionChrome`) | a second card design |
| An applied condition in a toolbar | `AppliedFilterChip` / `AppliedFilterChips` (three, then "+N more", then Clear all) | a `FilterChip` — that one is a choice, on or off |
| A policy's colour beside its name | `PolicyMarker` (a dot on a tint; `size="sm"` in a 28-high select, `pending` the legend's dashed ring) | a tag, a bar |
| Leave on a calendar or a lane | `LEAVE_CLASSES` / `leaveVars` (`lib/theme/leave.ts`): approved the fill, pending white with a dashed edge | the tag classes |
| An icon | `Icon` with a Hugeicons glyph, 16/20/24, stroke 1.75 | any other set |

A button's height is its `size` (sm 32, md 36, lg 44, `icon-sm | icon | icon-lg`); a destructive action
is `variant="destructive"` (red text), and only the confirm dialog's button is `destructive-confirm` (red
fill), with no accent button beside it. The dialog's title stays neutral.

### Steps: done is a tick, not a colour

From the designers' STEPS (2026-11-20; `hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-20-answers-from-design/7-product-wide/STEPS.md`,
measured in `AQ04a–c`), for every list of steps a person goes through — who approves a request (AQ04a–c), who signs a
document (the signing panel S07, the sign screen G02/G03, the guest page G09, "Next to sign" in G04). Colour alone
hides the order: with a green company colour "done" and "now" would both be green.

- **Sizes.** The step mark 16, the avatar 24 — the mark always smaller than the avatar; both on the name's first line.
- **Done:** a 16 circle in Mist with an Ink tick (10, stroke 2.5); the status line stays green (`status-approved-text`,
  "Manager · Approved Fri 20 Nov").
- **Now:** a 16 circle with a 1.5 px accent ring and the step number (600 10/12) in the accent; the name in the
  accent; the status in the pending text ("Waiting for you").
- **Not yet:** a 16 circle with a 1.5 px `border-strong` ring and the number in tertiary; the status tertiary.
- **No order** ("any 2 of 3"): no numbers — done keeps the tick circle, now is an 8 px accent dot, not yet an 8 px
  `border-strong` dot; the count on the right of the label row ("1 approved", 500, approved text).
- **No frame around the list**: a grey 13/18 label on top ("Who approves", "Who signs"), the steps one under another
  with a 1 px divider line between the marks and 14 between steps; the name 14/20 500, a 13/18 line under it
  (role · status).
- **The requester's own view** names nobody who has not decided: "Waiting for approval · 1 of 3 approved" (AQ04c).
- **Declined** stays red.

### Illustrations: no scene without an `-s` cut under 160

From the designers' hub fixes S (2026-11-19), for the whole product: **a scene without its own `-s` file is never
shown smaller than M 160.** SPEC § 10 allows S 96 only for the `-s` cuts, drawn without the thin support lines; an
uncut scene at 96 drops its 3-unit lines to 1.2 px, under the 2 px minimum. `<Illustration size="s">` enforces it:
it draws the scene's `-s` cut when one exists, and otherwise the scene itself at 160. **Home's widgets are the one
exception** (`keepSmall`, widgets Q): a widget card keeps 96. An illustration with a caption sits in the centre of
its free area, horizontally and vertically.

### Avatars: one rule for initials

From the designers' widgets fixes A1 and hub A9 (2026-11-19): without a photo, a person's initials sit on a tag tint
picked by their name and always the same for them — berry, ocean, indigo, teal, sand (`bronze`) or plum
(`avatarColor`, `lib/theme/tags.ts`), never gray — in **600 at about a third of the avatar** (22 → 8, 24 → 9, 28 → 10,
32 → 11, 36 → 12, 44 → 14, 48 → 15, 64 → 20). `AvatarFallback` draws it with the `text-initials` role, measured
against the avatar itself, so **a caller passes the person's `name` and never sets the initials' size**. Where faces
overlap, a 2 px ring in the card's colour (`ring-2 ring-card`; `PersonAvatar ring`).

## 6. The fence

`test/designSystemGuard.test.ts` reads every source file and fails on anything outside the system: the
old palette and Tailwind's colours, white/black, shadcn's colour names, Tailwind's type sizes, forbidden
weights and styles, Tailwind's radii and shadows, spinners and the old animation plugin, a raw HEX outside
the brand and accent files, the old theme's variables, another icon set, the old product name, a
hand-painted status panel, a hand-made error line, a button's height set by class, and three dots. Each
exception names its file and its reason. eslint's `RAW_HUE` rule says the first of these in the editor.

## 7. The owner's exceptions to SPEC

Settled by the owner and the designers on 2026-11-05 (`DECISIONS.md` §§ "The designers' fixes — what the owner settled"
and "The designers' answers on the fixes"). The package is not edited; **the code follows this list, not SPEC**, and
the designers take it into their next version. No new radius, width or type size came with it — everything else is the
package's own values.

- **The tooltip is light** (`desact/tooltip`): the overlay surface, a hairline, the level-2 shadow, 12/16 secondary text
  with an optional 500 title line, radius 10, 8 × 12 inside, max 240 wide, 8 px off, no arrow; 400 ms to show, none
  for the next while one is open (one provider at the root). No dark tooltip or dark floating hint anywhere.
- **A picked range of days is one look everywhere** (the designers' DATE-RANGE, 2026-11-20 — it replaced the soft
  band with `accent-muted` ends of 2026-11-05): filled accent circles at the ends, the band at 6 % accent from centre
  to centre, as tall as the circles, no rounded ends — FORMS_AND_FIELDS.md § 8. The team board keeps its own drag
  band per row, 4 px in, radius 8, the picked dates marked in the header.
- **The bulk-selection bar sits right above the list it acts on** (Ulia, 2026-11-17, product-wide; the owner took it
  2026-11-18): white, 48 high, radius 10, a hairline, and **its border and shadow tinted with the company colour** — an
  exception to SPEC § 7's "shadows are never tinted" as well as to § 13.5's dark floating bar. Inside: checkbox ·
  "3 selected" · a short divider · "Select all 7" … the actions on the right · a divider before the destructive one ·
  × at the end. Selected rows are accent-subtle. **Documents first**; it replaced the earlier rule (Mist, 40 px, in the
  toolbar's place — `ui/SelectionBar` as built) and every other list moves to it when it is next touched.
- **A list of records has no frame** (the same round): no card border or shadow around a table — only the column
  header and hairlines between rows. Documents first; other lists when they are next touched.
- **Dialogs are white**; the request time off dialog is the package's L (800) with 13/500 labels and a 16 px card.
- **Every positive action is the accent button** — inline helpers inside an editor ("Add option") stay secondary.
- **No noddo wordmark in the sidebar.**
- **Leave colours** (K01, `hris/design/screens/leave-colours`, Ulia 2026-11-19, taken by the owner the same day): **a
  palette of its own, apart from the tags.** A policy still stores a tag name (`TagColor`, the same twelve on the
  server), but leave is drawn from the `--leave-<name>-fill | -edge | -text` tokens in `globals.css`
  (`lib/theme/leave.ts`), never from `--tag-*`; the tags keep their own values for everything else a person colours. A
  policy picks from eleven in K01's order — Berry, Plum, Lilac, Indigo, Ocean, Teal, Olive, Mustard, Bronze, Orange,
  Cocoa — and a new one opens on the first nobody uses (the backend picks the same); **Gray is never offered: it is
  "Away"**, leave whose type the reader may not see. **Approved** is a pill in the fill with the text colour on it;
  **waiting for approval** is white with a 1.5 px **dashed** edge in the edge colour (no tint, no dots). The **policy
  marker** is **a dot on a tint** — a 16 px circle of the fill with an 8 px dot of the edge, no outline, 8 px before the
  name (`components/ui/PolicyMarker`; 14 with a 7 dot inside a 28-high select) — wherever a policy is named outside a
  calendar: it **replaced the 16 × 6 pill**. The picker (`components/ui/PolicyColorPicker`) draws the same marker at
  32. **A Scheduled status pill never stands beside a policy**: leave has no Scheduled status. The colour lives **on
  the policy**, not the leave type (D2, 2026-11-05). **The dark triplets are ours**: a deep fill with a light text at
  9 : 1 on it, and an edge within 4° of the designers' hue, 3 : 1 on a dark card and on its own fill, tuned until every
  two edges stay 6 apart (OKLab × 100) for normal vision and 2.5 under protanopia, deuteranopia or tritanopia —
  `test/leavePalette.test.ts`. Nine pairs of the designers' **light** edges fall under that floor (plum–indigo,
  mustard–bronze and bronze–orange for normal vision; olive with bronze and orange for protanopia; berry–teal and the
  three of mustard, bronze, orange for deuteranopia); the test lists them as known, and the name beside the colour
  carries the difference. The pale fills are not held to a distance at all — the dot and the name tell them apart.
  The four tag colours added on 2026-11-05 (Lilac, Orange, Mustard, Olive) stay in the tag palette, with their own
  test (`test/tagPalette.test.ts`).
- **The decision bar** ("Waiting on you" above a profile's tabs) is its own component, not a Banner.
- **Tabs are a segmented track, not an underline** (the designers' T1, 2026-11-19; `components/desact/tabs.tsx`, every
  tab row in the product). SPEC § 13.6 still draws the underline — for the next package version.

**Home's own exceptions** (the home redesign, `DECISIONS.md` § "The home redesign"; the specs' "Changes to SPEC"),
for Home only and as tokens of their own in `globals.css`: the widget card (radius 28, no border, `shadow-widget`), the
greeting at 52, widget titles at 20, big numbers 40–96 (**44 in every Small widget**), the AI box at radius 18, the
today tint at 12, the header band, and **pill-shaped** My profile, Edit home and segmented controls. Ordinary buttons
inside the widgets stay SPEC § 13.2. **Everything that is accent follows the company accent, decorations included** —
the band, the ring, the dots and the confetti. **Every name cut with … shows its whole text in a light tooltip.**

## 8. What is deliberately not built yet

- **Dark theme.** The tokens are installed and every component is on semantic roles, so it is a
  switch away; nothing switches it (SPEC: after launch).
- **Exit animations on overlays.** Dialogs, menus and panels animate in and not out — an exit animation
  under Radix left closed overlays mounted (`DECISIONS.md` § "The redesign onto noddo").
- **A workspace's own favicon and manifest name.** The manifest's `theme_color` follows the accent;
  the icon and the name stay noddo's (`NEED_TO_DISCUSS.md`).

## 9. Pages, and what a page carries

From the designers' company hub round (`hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-12-company-hub/PRODUCT-RULES.md`), taken by the owner on 2026-11-12 (CH7).

- **One sidebar.** A section never adds a second sidebar or a rail of its own; its sub-pages are tabs, links or a back
  link.
- **The accent band belongs to Home only.** No other page has a coloured header.
- **No boxes inside boxes.** A page has one hierarchy; its zones are separated by air and hairlines, not nested frames.
- **Reading and managing are apart.** The people who manage something do it on its own screen (the hub's *Manage hub*),
  entered by a quiet button; the reader's page carries no edit controls.
- **Section headings in two columns sit on one line**, at the same height.
- **Icons, not emoji**, for posts and pages: Hugeicons, or the post's own image as a thumbnail. An emoji appears only
  when an author types it at the start of a title — never in the product's own words, never as an icon.
- **Stat tiles are compact**: the label on top, the number, then one line of hint under it.

From the designers' answers of 2026-11-20 (`hris/design/handoffs/2026-11-20-answers-from-design/`):

- **The shell is exactly the window** (RC9). A banner — the demo's, impersonation's, the owner's email — sits on top,
  and the sidebar + main row fills the rest; only `main` scrolls, and only when its page is taller. A page that fills
  the area under the banners measures it in `cqh` (`main` is a size container: `h-[calc(100cqh-6rem)]`), never in
  `dvh`/`svh`, which count the banner and made every such page scroll by its height (`app/(app)/AppShell.tsx`).
- **Growing on wide windows** (AQ-20, `hris/design/handoffs/…/specs/first-run-grow`). Every `sign-in-*` and
  `first-run-*` screen with a colour pane or ring art grows with the window: the pane is its 1280 size × window ÷ 1280
  (the login's 520 pane, the first-experience card's 600 — 802 at 1710), never smaller than at 1280, and stops at 1920;
  the heading, the line under it and the rings or orbit scale with it (the board's `zoom: 1.336` at 1710), and the
  card's 12 margin does not. The welcome's ring strip is 62.5 % of the window — 900 at 1440, never smaller, 1200 at
  1920 — its rings, gaps and hang below the page scaled with it, and the nod never cut. In `styles/globals.css`:
  `--auth-grow` (`tan(atan2(100vw, 1280px))`, the window ÷ 1280 as a plain number) as the pane's `zoom`; the
  Appearance preview pins it to 1. Home is not part of it: four columns, 1200 at most (RC11).
- **A list of steps is a `StepList`** (`components/ui/StepList`, the designers' `7-product-wide/STEPS.md`): who signs,
  who approves. Done is a 16 Mist circle with an Ink tick, now a 16 accent ring with the number (the names in the
  accent), not yet a grey ring with the number; an unordered list ("any 2 of 3") has dots instead of numbers; a step
  never needed (`skipped` — the chain finished without it) is a grey dot in either. Marks 16,
  avatars 24, no frame, a grey label on top. Never a green "done" circle: with a green company colour done and now
  would look the same.
